standard_prerequisites.use: The induction step converts the isomorphism on every fibre into injectivity after tensoring the global sections with the local rings, which upgrades the displayed surjection to an isomorphism; openness of flatness and the two descent lemmas reduce the limit preserving question to a stage of the inverse system.

core_obligations: Prove the fpqc sheaf property: for an fpqc covering {T_i -> T}, pullback data and a point t, choose i and t_i over t with generic points xi_i and xi_t of the fibres, use flatness of O_{X_T,xi_t} -> O_{X_i,xi_i} and descent of finite projective modules to get that F at xi_t is free of rank p, then find an affine neighbourhood U of xi_t with a surjection from a free module and check that its fibre by fibre reduction is an isomorphism by the induction step lemma, after shrinking T so that U -> T is surjective with geometrically irreducible fibres (proof lines 6188-6235).

Prove the limit preserving property when F is of finite presentation: for a directed limit T = lim T_i over which the condition holds, let U be the open flat locus, observe it is smooth and surjective over T with geometrically irreducible fibres, shrink U to be quasi-compact, descend U and the flatness of the module on it to a stage i, use the resulting locally constant rank function to define the open and closed pieces (U_i)_p and their open quasi-compact images V_i in T_i, and since the image of T lies in V_i find i' with T_{i'} -> T_i factoring through V_i, so that the condition descends to the stage i' (proof lines 6237-6267).
proof_roadmap: Sheaf property: descend local freeness to the limit point through the flat local map of stalks, then upgrade a surjection to an isomorphism by the induction step lemma (proof lines 6188-6235).
Limit preserving: descend the flat locus to a stage, use the rank stratification and the open images in the base to read off a stage where the condition already holds (proof lines 6237-6267).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the functor H_p assigning to a base change the property that the pullback of a module is free of rank p at every generic point of every fibre is an fpqc sheaf, and is limit preserving when the module is of finite presentation (statement lines 6178-6186, tag 05MS). The proof has two genuinely different halves: the sheaf half descends local freeness to the limit point through the flat local map of stalks and then has to upgrade a surjection from a free module to an isomorphism by checking the reduction fibre by fibre, using the induction step lemma; the limit preserving half descends the flat locus and its rank stratification to a stage and uses the open images in the base to find a stage at which the condition already holds. The second half is the substance, so the claim is H2.
